text: Two short notes on the README, each with its reason beside it.

markdown:
<to-human>
Keep the README short.
</to-human>

<insight>
A README is read in two modes. Someone deciding whether the project is for them reads the first screen and stops; someone already committed comes back to it, again and again, for one command they half remember.

A short README serves both. The first reader gets the summary without wading through setup detail, and the second reader finds the command without scrolling past paragraphs written for the first.

Length also decays. Every section is a promise to keep in step with the code, and the sections nobody reads are the ones nobody notices going stale, until a newcomer follows them and fails.

Detail that matters still has a home: the docs directory, the scripts themselves, the comments beside the code. The README points at those places rather than repeating them.

So the bar for a README section is that most readers need it on most visits. Anything that fails that bar moves out, and a link stays behind.
</insight>

<to-human>
Put the commands first.
</to-human>

<insight>
Readers scan for a command before they read prose.
</insight>
